recentItems.title: Max B Sold WHAT To His Mom!? 😳
My Involvement In Carmen Bryan's Lawsuit Against NORE...
Nas' Babymother Carmen Bryan, Who's Suing Nore for Sexual Assault, Tells Her Life Story (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback from 2017, Carmen Bryan opened up to VladTV about being at the center of Jay-Z and Nas’ legendary beef. She explained that after breaking up with Nas, she became friends with Jay-Z before the two eventually started dating. Carmen denied rumors that she was the reason behind Jay-Z and Nas’ feud and revealed that she confronted both rappers about their issues. More recently, Carmen reacted to allegations involving Jay-Z, which brought renewed attention to details of their past relationship discussed in her book.

recentItems.title: Lul Tim on First Conversation with NBA YoungBoy After Killing King Von (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit Lul Tim discussing his involvement in Quando Rondo and NBA YoungBoy’s collaborative mixtape, 3860. Vlad praised the project, calling it his favorite work from both artists and comparing their chemistry to Kobe and Shaq.

Despite NBA YoungBoy’s initial reluctance to release the project, label pressure and Quando Rondo’s persistence ultimately led to the mixtape’s release. Lul Tim explained how music provides an outlet for self-expression and detailed his own contributions to the project, including a significant verse on the opening track.

Tim also recalled a pivotal conversation with NBA YoungBoy following his release from jail, when YoungBoy encouraged him not to worry about public perception and reassured him about his legal situation.

Vlad breaks down Carmen Bryan’s sexual assault lawsuit against N.O.R.E., detailing her allegations from a 1999 nightclub encounter during promotion for his second album and the reported aftermath involving Nas, Jay-Z, and their daughter Destiny’s birthday party. He explains how New York City’s Victims of Gender-Motivated Violence Protection Law may affect the statute of limitations, and why Bryan says the Cassie lawsuit against Diddy triggered renewed trauma. Vlad also responds to speculation about his involvement, denying any role in the case and clarifying his past interview history with Carmen Bryan. The discussion also covers Rolling Stone and TMZ coverage, possible settlement strategy, N.O.R.E.’s legal exposure, and Vlad’s ongoing feud with the Drink Champs host. Later, Vlad addresses N.O.R.E.’s wife threatening defamation action over comments about her race, ethnicity, and appearance, referencing Love & Hip Hop, Marriage Boot Camp, and public figure standards.

recentItems.title: Nicholas Irving: on Why Nobody Powerful Gets Touched over the Epstein Files (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving returns to VladTV with Shawn Prez for a wide-ranging conversation on war, media fatigue, and why the Jeffrey Epstein files remain a major unanswered story. Irving argues that endless news cycles, rising costs, and political distractions have worn down public attention, comparing today’s climate to Occupy Wall Street and citing a Princeton study on voter influence.  

The discussion turns to Donald Trump, MAGA promises to “drain the swamp,” the FBI, redacted documents, and the lack of arrests beyond Ghislaine Maxwell despite Epstein’s long history of abuse allegations. Irving and Prez question why powerful figures in politics, Hollywood, and business have not faced accountability, drawing comparisons to Watergate and broader mistrust in government. They also discuss the ongoing war, an expired memorandum of understanding in August, and whether public exhaustion is being used to keep Americans from demanding answers.

recentItems.title: Chingy Says: Spoke with Shaka Zulu after He Killed Someone in Self-Defense (Part 8)

Part 1: https://youtu.be/tDpGD3Z34Sc
--------

Chingy sits down with VladTV to break down the realities of music industry contracts, from early production deals to the leverage that comes after hit records. The St. Louis rapper reflects on getting only $9,000 upfront but later balancing it out with a $3 million publishing check, crediting Shaka Zulu—Ludacris’ manager and co-owner of Disturbing Tha Peace—for knowing how to navigate the business. Chingy also addresses Shaka Zulu’s Buckhead shooting outside Apt 4B, saying he spoke with him afterward and believes the video showed clear self-defense in the death of Martez Benton. The conversation also touches on Hit-Boy’s frustrations with long-term deals, records with J.Lo, Flo Rida, Eminem, Lil Wayne and “N****s in Paris,” plus Chingy’s take on the Pooh Shiesty and Gucci Mane contract controversy involving Big Scarr and alleged robbery accusations.

recentItems.title: Norteño Shot Caller Mario Sanchez on Why Mexicans Won't Take Paid Hits Against Blacks (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/-pWadYhoSkc
--------
Norteño figure Mario Sanchez joins Vlad to break down the Keefe D case tied to the killing of Tupac Shakur, reacting to the rapid jury verdict and the role of public statements, social media, and self-incrimination in major criminal cases. The conversation also addresses long-running rumors surrounding Sean “Puffy” Combs and an alleged $1 million bounty, while Sanchez explains how paid hits can exist inside prison and street organizations. He draws a clear distinction between Mexican factions such as Norteños and Sureños, Black gangs like Crips and Bloods, and the Mafia’s internal code, saying trust issues and historic friction often keep groups from crossing racial lines for contract violence. Sanchez also reflects on the divide between prison politics and street life, emphasizing that the two worlds operate differently.

recentItems.title: Max B: I Signed to Jim Jones in 2005 for $100K Advance, Blew the Money in 90 Days (Part 3)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 2: https://youtu.be/J_JvDb3JAX0
Part 1: https://youtu.be/FoBBj-6j544
--------
Max B breaks down how Cam’ron connected him with Jim Jones during the rise of Bird Gang and Dipset’s mid-2000s Harlem run. In this VladTV interview, the Wave God recalls signing to Jim Jones around late 2005, receiving a $100,000 advance, and spending it within 90 days after coming home. He details the studio energy behind Jim’s *Harlem: Diary of a Summer*, claiming he helped write multiple records, including credited work on tracks like “Baby Girl” and “G’s Up.” Max also reflects on the album’s commercial impact, its No. 5 debut on the Billboard 200, and the independent rap climate that helped Jim Jones move hundreds of thousands of units. From dark studio sessions to Miami memories and working alongside legends like Pete Rock, Max B revisits a pivotal chapter in New York hip-hop history.

recentItems.title: Charleston White on Boosie, Lil Durk, Yella Beezy, Mo3, Getting Arrested (Full Interview)
recentItems.description:
Watch the FULL uncensored interview early - become a VladTV YouTube Member now:
https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Charleston White returns to VladTV to discuss several major hip-hop criminal cases, including the Lil Durk trial, the Mo3 murder case, and Yella Beezy's legal situation, before addressing his own recent arrest in Texas.

Charleston weighs in on Lil Durk's trial and predicts a quick verdict, arguing that the prosecution has presented a strong case while criticizing the defense strategy. He also addresses his own ongoing issues with Mob James and explains why he stands behind his actions throughout their public feud.
The conversation then shifts to the Mo3 murder case, including the alleged roles of Kewon White and Devin Brown. Charleston shares his thoughts on the evidence and explains why he remains skeptical of Yella Beezy's claims of innocence. He and Vlad also discuss Boosie's dispute with Rod Wave, with Charleston emphasizing accountability, honoring agreements, and maintaining respect when money and business are involved.

Later, Charleston explains his recent arrest in the Dallas area stemming from a warrant related to an expired driver's license and marijuana possession. He discusses his Texas medical marijuana status, says he was released within hours, and clarifies that he is dealing with misdemeanor charges rather than facing significant jail time.

Charleston also reacts to the unusual case of Dejon Love, who was accused of defrauding women while allegedly pretending to be an NFL player. Charleston questions the severity of the case, compares Love's alleged tactics to behavior commonly seen in dating, and jokes that Love should turn his experiences into a book.
